title: Evolutionary Trajectory of Radioresistance in Lung Cancer Brain Metastasis Organoids
author: Chen, Gao, et al.
materials: TF activity was inferred from gene expression data using the DoRothEA (Discriminant Regulon Expression Analysis) package coupled with the decoupleR algorithm [21, 22]. Only regulons with high confidence (confidence levels A, B, and C) were included. The weighted mean method (run_wmean) was used to compute single-cell TF activity scores. Differential TF activity analysis was performed to identify key regulators driving the response to radiotherapy. Functional enrichment (GO/KEGG) of the target genes regulated by these differential TFs was conducted to elucidate their biological functions. Furthermore, TF-target regulatory networks were constructed and visualized to highlight master regulators in the post-radiation context.

steps.title: Generate scRNA‑seq library
steps.instruction: Prepare single‑cell suspensions from patient‑derived organoids and process them into single‑cell RNA‑seq libraries using the manufacturer’s high‑throughput platform, following the standard instructions provided with the kit.

steps.title: Sequence libraries
steps.instruction: Run the prepared libraries on a high‑throughput sequencing system to obtain raw sequencing reads.

steps.title: Align reads and build matrix
steps.instruction: Align raw reads to the human reference genome GRCh38 and quantify gene expression to generate a gene‑expression matrix using a standard upstream bioinformatics pipeline.

steps.title: Apply quality control filters
steps.instruction: Retain cells that (1) have between 200 and 6,000 detected genes and (2) have mitochondrial gene percentage < 15 %; predict and remove doublets with DoubletFinder.

steps.title: Normalize data and select HVGs
steps.instruction: Log‑normalize the filtered matrix (Seurat NormalizeData), then identify the top 2,000 highly variable genes using FindVariableFeatures with method = “vst”.

steps.title: Integrate pre‑ and post‑RT samples
steps.instruction: Use the Harmony algorithm to integrate the pre‑radiotherapy and post‑radiotherapy datasets and mitigate batch effects.

steps.title: Dimensionality reduction and clustering
steps.instruction: Perform principal component analysis, retain the top 30 PCs, construct a neighbor graph (FindNeighbors), cluster cells with FindClusters at resolution = 0.5, and visualize the results with UMAP.

steps.title: Annotate cell types
steps.instruction: Assign cell‑type identities based on canonical marker expression: EPCAM, KRT18, KRT19 (Epithelial/Tumor); CD3D, CD3E (T cells); CD68, LYZ (Myeloid); CD79A, MS4A1 (B cells); COL1A1, DCN (Fibroblasts).

steps.title: Perform inferCNV analysis
steps.instruction: Run inferCNV (v1.12.0) using T cells and myeloid cells as the reference baseline; set denoise = TRUE, HMM = TRUE, cutoff = 0.1; calculate a CNV score for each cell as the mean‑squared deviation from the reference across all genomic windows.

steps.title: Infer transcription factor activity
steps.instruction: Apply DoRothEA together with the decoupleR algorithm, include regulons with confidence levels A, B, and C, compute single‑cell TF activity scores using the weighted‑mean method (run_wmean), and identify differentially active TFs; subsequently perform GO/KEGG enrichment on target genes of the differential TFs.

steps.title: Reconstruct pseudotime trajectory
steps.instruction: Using Monocle 2, convert the raw count matrix of epithelial cells into a CellDataSet object, select ordering genes with q‑value < 0.01, build the trajectory with the DDRTree algorithm, and order cells along pseudotime to define a “Sensitive State” (early) and a “Resistant State” (late).

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze results with GraphPad Prism (v10.0.3) and R (v4.1.2); ensure each experiment has at least three independent replicates; report data as mean ± SD or SEM; compare two groups using a two‑sided Student’s t‑test or Wilcoxon rank‑sum test as appropriate; consider p < 0.05 statistically significant.
